MiSTer × Stream Deck

A button for your
next game.

Button Goblin turns an Elgato Stream Deck into a control panel for your MiSTer FPGA gaming system. Press an animated character button to launch a console or favorite game, navigate menus, or run Update All.

Set up your deck →

Runs directly on MiSTer over USB. Use a six-key Mini, a 15-key MK.2, or both.

Choose your deck

Stream Deck Mini

Six buttons across six pages. Consoles, Update All, and navigation fit into a compact setup.

See the Mini buttons →

Stream Deck MK.2

Fifteen buttons across two pages. Keep your console launchers together, then switch to menu shortcuts.

See the MK.2 buttons →

You’ll need a MiSTer, a supported Stream Deck, and a USB data connection to MiSTer’s USB host hub. No Elgato desktop software or Python is needed on MiSTer.

Page 2 / Installation

Install in a few steps

Download the package for your deck, copy it to your MiSTer, and run its Enable script. The same Dual package supports MK.2 alone or both decks together.

Your deckDownloadEnable script
MiniMini packageButtonGoblin_Mini_Enable.sh
MK.2Dual packageButtonGoblin_Enable.sh
BothDual packageButtonGoblin_Both_Enable.sh
  1. Download and extract your package.

    Use the table above. Keep the extracted files together.

  2. Copy the complete Scripts contents to MiSTer.

    Merge the package’s Scripts contents into /media/fat/Scripts/ on your SD card, including the hidden .config folder. On macOS, show hidden files with Command–Shift–period; on Windows, use View → Show → Hidden items.

  3. Connect your deck and run Enable.

    Connect to MiSTer’s USB host hub with a data-capable cable. Open MiSTer’s Scripts menu and run the Enable script listed above. Button Goblin starts now and automatically at boot.

  4. Launch your first console.

    Wait for the startup artwork to finish, then press a console button whose core is installed. For Mini controls, open the Mini guide. MK.2 controls are in the tabs above.

Bring your own games and cores. Cores, BIOS files, games, and favorites are separate installs. Update All is optional and must already exist at /media/fat/Scripts/update_all.sh. The SNES and Simpsons defaults use specific game shortcuts; check their paths or change them in the editor.

Updating an existing installation?

Wait for Update All to finish. Back up your layout or saved editor project, run the matching Disable script, copy the new files, then run Enable. Replacing supplied configurations can overwrite your custom buttons.

MK.2 cable and USB connection details

Connect it with a USB-A–to–USB-C data cable

Plug the USB-C end into the Stream Deck MK.2 and the USB-A end into an available USB port on MiSTer’s connected USB hub. This single cable carries power and button/display data. Use a cable rated for USB 2.0 data or faster; a charge-only cable will not let MiSTer detect or control the deck.

If your deck came with a USB-C–to–USB-C cable, use a suitable USB-A–to–USB-C data cable for MiSTer’s USB-A ports, or a data-capable adapter. Box contents have changed over time; check the cable you have. Use a short, reliable cable and a properly powered hub if connections are unstable.

Hardware reference: Elgato MK.2 specifications and included cables. Connect through the USB host hub, not a power-only port.

Page 3 / Shortcut layout

Page two: navigate and map controllers

Keep your console buttons on page one. Hold button 15, Stay Puft, for one second to open this shortcut page. Release the button, then use the arrows, Menu, Enter, Space, and Escape. Each shortcut has its own animation. Held buttons turn green until release; Back morphs into Stay Puft every fifth cycle and returns to page one when released. Map an Xbox controller

  1. Open the shortcut page, then press Menu.

    Use arrows and Enter to open MiSTer’s controller-mapping option. Its exact location depends on the menu/core currently loaded.

  2. Respond with your Xbox controller.

    Press the controller buttons requested by MiSTer. The Stream Deck supplies keyboard shortcuts; it does not replace or pair the controller.

  3. Skip, finish, or cancel.

    Use Space to skip an entry, Enter to finish mapping, or Escape to cancel.

  4. Return to your games.

    Press Back to restore page one. Brightness is retained, and Update All continues if it was already running.

Customize page two

Open editor/index.html and choose 2 · Shortcuts in the page selector, or edit buttons-shortcuts.conf directly. Action names are space, menu, enter, up, down, left, right, escape, back, and none. Keep a Back button available.

# Physical button 11 = configuration key 10
key.10.label=SPACE
key.10.action=space
key.10.image=custom/page2_10.jpg
key.10.trigger=press

Safe page changes

Switching clears queued launches and releases held shortcuts. Inputs wait while the new page finishes drawing; already-held buttons must be released before they can act on that page.

Restart and configuration reload return to page one. USB reconnect retains the current page.

Page 4 / Everyday controls

Update All, brightness & startup

Button 14 · Update All

Install Update All separately at /media/fat/Scripts/update_all.sh. Pressing button 14 runs it in the background. Repeated presses during that run do not start another copy.

Ready

Press button 14 to start your installed updater.

Updating

The arrow circles while Update All runs in the background.

Finished

A green pulse settles to gray; the pulse repeats about once a minute.

Failed

Check the logs, fix the cause, then press again.

The finished or failed state remains until the next attempt. Update All continues while page two is visible; return to page one to see its status. Restarting the launcher clears it. Supported Update All builds receive non-interactive settings; use MiSTer’s Scripts menu when you want the updater’s interactive settings.

To see progress over SSH:

tail -f /tmp/buttongoblin.script.log

The log retains recent output up to 128 KiB. Update All has a one-hour deadline. Stopping or enabling the launcher stops a launcher-owned updater, so wait until it finishes before restarting or upgrading.

Button 15 · Stay Puft brightness

Each short tap and release advances to the next higher level, then wraps back to the first:

10%25%50%75%100%

The default is 65%, so the first press selects 75%. The cycle never turns the display fully off. Restarting restores the configured brightness. Hold this button for one second to open page two. A long press does not also change brightness.

First connection · MiSTer mosaic

A stationary title screen fades in, holds, then fades out before the normal animated buttons fade in. Inputs are ignored during this sequence. Reconnecting USB restores the buttons without replaying it.

Page 5 / Customize & help

Assign icons, games & scripts

Open the MK.2 editor on your computer and choose the console or shortcut page. For the six-key deck, use the Mini editor. Export includes both configurations and their artwork. Save project keeps both pages; older single-page projects import with the default shortcut page. Keep page-one key.14.action=cycle for the brightness tap/hold page switch. The editor prepares files locally; it does not connect to MiSTer or execute the scripts you assign.

  1. Select a page-one key and set its action.

    Choose launch for a core/game, script for a shell script, update_all for the updater, or cycle for brightness. Other controls include dim, bright, reload, restart and none.

  2. Choose the target and input trigger.

    Use a core .rbf, game launcher .mgl, or arcade .mra. Relative paths start at /media/fat; absolute paths work too. Choose press, release, or hold. Hold fires once per hold, with a configurable 100–10,000 ms delay.

  3. Choose your artwork.

    Use a console preset or upload an image/GIF for Normal, Request and Error. Keep pixel art crisp using the editor’s nearest-neighbor conversion. Changing a label does not replace text already drawn into an image.

  4. Save your editable project, then export.

    Save project downloads JSON; Open project restores it. The editor does not automatically retain your work when closed. Export for MiSTer downloads configuration and artwork, without the launcher binary.

  5. Apply the exported layout.

    After any running updater finishes, run Disable. Merge the export’s Scripts contents onto the SD card, then run Enable. Keep the installed launcher binary. Reset layout restores animated defaults; Use default restores a static icon.

Launch a favorite game

key.1.action=launch
key.1.target=_@Favorites/My Game.mgl
key.1.trigger=press

Use the real filename from your MiSTer. A raw ROM path cannot be sent directly to the core loading interface.

Run your own script

key.0.action=script
key.0.target=Scripts/MyScript.sh
key.0.trigger=hold
key.0.hold_ms=700

Ordinary scripts run through /bin/sh, with no extra arguments and a 60-second deadline. Only one script or updater runs at a time.

Core wildcard paths select the lexicographically latest matching filename. Use an exact path when you want to pin a particular core. GIF imports are limited to 1024×1024, 128 source frames and 30 seconds; exported animations are limited to 32 frames and the total configured image cache to 4 MiB.

Files

A tidy installation

The app lives directly under Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/, with no versioned subfolder. Only Enable and Disable appear as management scripts in MiSTer’s Scripts menu.

LocationPurpose
/media/fat/Scripts/ButtonGoblin_Enable.shValidate, start/restart the launcher and enable boot startup.
/media/fat/Scripts/ButtonGoblin_Disable.shStop the launcher and disable boot startup; retain configuration and artwork.
/media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/buttongoblin-misterNative launcher binary.
/media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/buttons.confPage-one actions, paths, triggers and brightness.
/media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/buttons-shortcuts.confPage-two shortcut actions and icons.
/media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/icons/Prepared JPEGs, animations and GIF previews.
/media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/extras/Additional management and diagnostics scripts.
/media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/source/Source code, artwork tools and tests; build tools run on a computer.
Deck_Editor/ on your computerOffline configuration editor.

Show hidden files when copying. On Windows, turn on View → Show → Hidden items; on macOS Finder, press Command–Shift–period. The .config directory contains the actual application.

Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting & recovery

Page two does not appear or shortcuts fail

Hold Stay Puft for at least one second. Confirm that buttons-shortcuts.conf, its artwork, and the updated binary were copied. Keep page-one key.14.action=cycle. Keyboard shortcuts require /dev/uinput; check diagnostics for a virtual-keyboard error.

No response or blank buttons

Check power and the USB connection, confirm the hidden app folder was copied, then run Disable followed by Enable. Let the startup fade finish. If necessary, reconnect the Stream Deck and check diagnostics.

A console or game does not launch

Check the configured filename, core, BIOS and game installation. SNES uses the specific Donkey Kong Country favorite; Genesis uses MegaDrive. A SENT indicator means the command was written, not that MiSTer finished loading it.

Update All shows FAILED or does not start

Confirm /media/fat/Scripts/update_all.sh and Bash are installed. Check the script log below. Another script may already be running. Fix the issue and press again, or run the updater interactively from MiSTer’s Scripts menu.

Artwork is missing, stale or flickering

Use a fresh export from the matching editor, copy its artwork along with buttons.conf, and restart with Disable/Enable after the updater finishes. Imported GIFs must be converted by the editor; pointing a runtime image entry at an ordinary GIF is insufficient. Try a powered USB hub if uploads are unstable.

How does recovery work?

A supervisor restarts crashed workers with a 1–30 second backoff and detects a 20-second stall. USB errors trigger reconnection. Held keys after reconnect wait for release, and queued actions are cleared to avoid replay. Hardware or driver faults can still require unplugging or rebooting.

Will animations affect MiSTer?

The native worker uses prepared frames, with no GIF decoding on MiSTer and no growing frame queue. USB writes and image memory are bounded. The service uses low CPU priority and requests idle disk priority where supported. Static icons produce the lowest USB traffic; scripts you launch can have their own resource demands.

Collect diagnostics over SSH

sh /media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/extras/ButtonGoblin_Diagnostics.sh

The report is saved at /media/fat/Scripts/.config/buttongoblin/diagnostics.txt. These temporary logs are also useful:

/tmp/buttongoblin.log
/tmp/buttongoblin.script.log
/tmp/buttongoblin_start.log
/tmp/buttongoblin_boot.log
